full_judgment:
6. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, after placing the impugned order and other materials on record submitted that Court of appeal below acted illegally in staying operation of the order of temporary mandatory .injunction. He further submitted that Court of appeal below failed to appreciate the urgency in the matter when the Court's order was violated by the opposite party with the assistance of the police and in spite of the appeal being ready sat over the matter for the last 6(six) months to the prejudice of his client. 

 12. In that view of the matter the order of stay passed by-the learned District Judge on 12.11.94 is liable to be set aside. The learned District Judge might have assumed jurisdiction under an erroneous view of the law but the dilatory manner in which he dealt with the matter shows that he failed to appreciate the urgency of a matter in respect of an order of temporary mandatory injunction. Temporary mandatory injunction is passed by a Court when it is satisfied that a party taking the law in his own hands altered the status quo in respect of the suit property existing at the time of filing of the suit. No one how high so ever can take the law in his own hands specially when the matter is pending in a Court of law. A party altering the status quo existing at the time of filing of the suit or proceeding must be compelled to restore the status quo. Court of appeal below should have decided the appeal when both the parties appeared and the lower court record was before that Court. But without doing that he merely stayed the operation of the order of the trial Court and sat over the matter. Such lethargic attitude on the part of an experienced Court like the District Judge is undesirable.
